Install tobi-try on Omarchy

try is a small command-line tool for people who spin up throwaway coding experiments constantly. Instead of hunting through a messy folder tree, you type a short name and it either fuzzy-jumps you into a matching, previously-created experiment directory or instantly creates a new date-prefixed one (like 2025-08-17-redis-experiment) and cds your shell into it. It can also clone a git repo straight into a new dated directory.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add tobi-try
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 1.10.1-3:
    pacman -Qi tobi-try

Open and use tobi-try

tobi-try has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql tobi-try | grep /usr/bin/

tobi-try requirements and compatibility

  • Ruby installed
  • Bash, Zsh, or Fish shell integration to enable the auto-cd behavior

Dependencies Omarchy installs for you

  • ruby

Pricing and license

Free and open source. License: MIT.

Uninstall tobi-try

omarchy pkg drop tobi-try

Frequently asked questions

How do I install tobi-try on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add tobi-try. The download is 26.3 KB and it takes 80.5 KB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is tobi-try free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed MIT.

How do I uninstall tobi-try?

Run omarchy pkg drop tobi-try. It removes the package from your system.

What does tobi-try depend on?

The package declares 1 dependency: ruby. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is tobi-try a desktop app?

No. tobi-try has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is tobi-try in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as tobi-try (version 1.10.1-3) in the official Omarchy package repository. Tobias Lütke makes it. Project site: https://github.com/tobi/try.
